summary: Six iterations have confirmed that the bracket K=1 hierarchical search algorithm correctly identifies the optimal tensor-parallelism configuration across all tested hardware (H100, A100-SXM, L40S) and request rates, with all quantitative predictions matching observations to within 0.01%. The core discovery is a universal, physics-grounded rule: the optimal TP degree transitions from TP=8 at low rates to TP=4 at high rates, and the crossover request rate scales inversely with GPU memory bandwidth (H100 at ~125 req/s, A100-SXM at ~200 req/s, L40S at ~450 req/s). What remains is validating the algorithm's behavior at the L40S crossover boundary and testing whether the crossover rate can be predicted analytically from hardware specs alone.
key_points: All 4 arms in iteration 6 confirmed exactly: 25/25 seed combinations selected TP=8/1inst on A100-SXM at rate=100 (margins 3.7–5.2% for llama, 2.5% for qwen); the qwen rate=200 crossover was pinned to 0.001% TP tie; bracket K=1 achieved evals_to_best=4 (TP=8 winner) or 3 (TP=4 winner) deterministically across all seeds versus flat TPE's median of 6 with high variance (range 1–18).

Known unknowns heading into iteration 7: (1) The exact A100-SXM crossover rate for llama (somewhere between 100 and 500 req/s, not yet narrowed). (2) Whether the inverse-bandwidth crossover model is quantitatively predictive enough to skip simulation — e.g., can we derive 'crossover_rate = k / bandwidth' with a fitted constant k? (3) Whether bracket K=1 handles L40S llama correctly at its ~450 req/s crossover, the highest crossover rate observed and the most challenging for the algorithm since TP=4 margin is only 2.1%.

Recommended next iteration: (1) Run bracket K=1 on L40S llama at rate=450–500 to test behavior near the tightest observed margin (2.1%), which is the most likely failure case for the 1% threshold heuristic. (2) Probe intermediate rates (150, 250, 350) on A100-SXM llama to narrow its crossover and check whether the bandwidth-scaling model holds for a second model/hardware combination. (3) Optionally, prototype a 'blis search' subcommand that embeds bracket K=1 natively, removing the external Python wrapper.
